scenes.summary: Bob surveys the Delta Eridani system, identifies a promising habitable planet and a rich asteroid belt, and notices suspicious nighttime fires on Delta Eridani 4.
Bob establishes mining, communications, clone-production, and early-warning infrastructure in the system while reflecting uneasily on clone divergence.
Bob deploys exploration drones to Delta Eridani 4, studies its rich biosphere, and confirms the presence of fire-using intelligent natives.

events.text: Bob surveys Delta Eridani, identifies a habitable rocky world and a resource-rich asteroid belt, and begins establishing mining, communications, defense, and clone-production infrastructure there.
Bob discovers intelligent pre-industrial native life on Delta Eridani 4, removing it from consideration as a human colony target.

summary.one_line: Bob reaches Delta Eridani, starts building up the system, and discovers intelligent alien life on its promising habitable world.
summary.paragraph: Bob arrives in Delta Eridani and finds exactly the kind of system he had hoped for: a stable star, ten planets, a habitable-zone rocky world, and an unusually rich asteroid belt. He quickly surveys Delta Eridani 4, notices suspicious nighttime fires, and then pauses long enough to establish mining operations, an early-warning drone network, a communications station, and the beginnings of a clone facility. While exploring the planet with camouflaged drones, he is delighted by a complex Earthlike biosphere full of convergent analogues to insects, mammals, birds, and snakes. The chapter culminates with Bob confirming that the fires belong to intelligent native beings, making Delta Eridani 4 unsuitable for human colonization but marking a major first-contact discovery.
events: Bob surveys the Delta Eridani system and is thrilled to find a highly promising arrangement of planets, including a habitable-zone rocky world.
He performs an orbital scan of Delta Eridani 4, notices suspicious points of light on the night side, and postpones investigating them until after finishing his resource survey.
Bob completes the asteroid-belt survey, finds excellent mining prospects, and sets up mining equipment, transport drones, an early-warning observation network, and a communications station.
He reflects uneasily on how much his first cohort of clones has already diverged in personality and admits he is nervous about eventually making more Bobs.
Unable to resist exploring, Bob deploys camouflaged drones to Delta Eridani 4 and studies a rich alien ecosystem full of familiar-looking evolutionary analogues.
At night, his drones locate the source of the fires and reveal groups of native beings tending them and apparently speaking, convincing Bob he has found intelligent alien life.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from exuberant explorer's joy and mild loneliness to awe and triumph as he realizes he has found intelligent alien life.

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
Bob detects apparent nuclear detonations on Earth after hearing of escalating conflict, leaving the scale of the war and Sol's survival uncertain.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Butterworth reveals that the USE probe launched after Heaven-1 but was never heard from again, leaving its fate unknown.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.

recent_events.text: Milo finishes surveying Omicron Eridani, secures the system for future colonists, and heads for 82 Eridani.
Riker and Homer wipe out the Brazilian force in Sol and save Earth from four extinction-level asteroid strikes.
Bill and Garfield achieve a breakthrough by successfully testing real-time subspace communication.
Riker's mysterious hail turns out to be surviving USE forces, who ask for Bob help to build colony ships and evacuate humanity from dying Earth.
Bob reaches Delta Eridani, starts building up the system, and discovers intelligent alien life on its promising habitable world.
